outputs.exact_statement: The promise problem above is QMA-hard under deterministic classical polynomial-time many-one reductions for $c=1$. The reduction can produce instances with $b-a\ge1$.

There is a QMA-complete promise problem whose Hamiltonians are $$H_{\rm in}=\sum_{e=LR}J_e h^s_{LR}$$ on finite, nonwrapping subgraphs of the square lattice, with no one-qubit terms. The signed weights $J_e$ are rational. The number of vertices and edges, the lattice extent, the weight magnitudes, and the threshold magnitudes are bounded by fixed polynomials in the source size $n\geq2$. The rational thresholds $a_s<b_s$ have separation $\delta_s=b_s-a_s\geq1/\operatorname{poly}(n)$.

All the sites $p_i$ are distinct. Every pair is either at distance one or at distance at least $\sqrt2$. The complete set $\mathcal C$ of unit-distance pairs consists of:*

1.  *$L A_e$, $A_e R$, and $A_e B_e$ for a negative source edge;*

2.  *$L A_e$, $A_e B_e$, and $B_e R$ for a positive source edge;*

3.  *$B_e A_f$ for two consecutive positive source edges $e,f$ on the same original lattice line.*

*Thus every interaction of $H_+$ is a contact. Its weight on a contact will be denoted $K_{ij}\geq0$, using $K_{ij}=0$ for contacts in the third class.

The operators $h_i$ are self-adjoint on $H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, with form domain $H^1(\mathbb R^3)$. Each has a simple ground eigenvalue $\lambda_i$ and a real, positive, normalized eigenfunction $\psi_i$. There is a constant $g>0$ such that the remaining spectrum is at least $\lambda_i+g$. For $\phi_i(y)=\pi^{-1/2}e^{-r_i}$, $$|\lambda_i+1/2|\le C\frac mD,\qquad
 \|\psi_i-\phi_i\|_{H^2}\le C\frac mD.
 \label{eq:wells-h2}$$ Moreover, for derivative orders $j=0,1,2$, $$\|D^jW_i\|_\infty\le C\frac m{D^{j+1}},
 \qquad 0\le W_i\le\frac{100m}{D}.
 \label{eq:wells-field-bounds}$$ These assertions hold before tuning and uniformly throughout $[1,4]^m$.

With centers and rounded charges fixed, for every choice of the other parameters, $\lambda_i(\rho_i=1)<-1/2<\lambda_i(\rho_i=4)$. For $1\le a<b\le4$, holding the other parameters fixed, $$c q'(b-a)\le\lambda_i(b)-\lambda_i(a)\le Cq'(b-a).
 \label{eq:wells-own-slope}$$ If instead $\rho_i$ is held fixed, then $$|\lambda_i(\rho)-\lambda_i(\widetilde\rho)|
 \le Cq'\frac m{D^2}\|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_\infty.
 \label{eq:wells-other-slope}$$

Uniformly for all $\rho\in[1,4]^m$, $$|\psi_i(y)|\le C\exp[-.99(r_i-.01D)],
 \label{eq:wells-tail}$$ and, for sufficiently large $D$, $$\|\psi_i\|_{H^1(\{r_i>.65D\})}\le e^{-.61D}.
 \label{eq:wells-h1-tail}$$

Suppose $u$ is bounded on the unit ball in $\mathbb R^3$ and satisfies $\Delta u=Fu$ there, where $$\|\partial^\beta F\|_\infty\le A^{|\beta|+1}|\beta|!
 \quad\text{for every multi-index }\beta.
 \label{eq:wells-analytic-coefficient}$$ There is a constant $A_1$, depending only on $A$, such that $$\max_{|\alpha|=k}\|\partial^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(B_{1/4})}
 \le \|u\|_{L^2(B_1)}A_1^{k+1}k!.
 \label{eq:wells-analytic-derivatives}$$ On a sufficiently small fixed ball about the origin, Taylor polynomials consequently have geometrically decreasing errors in both value and first derivative, with constants depending only on $A$.

For each $i$, each rational choice of centers and secondary parameters, and each sufficiently large $D$, one can explicitly construct a space $\mathcal V_i\subset H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ of rational piecewise polynomials, of dimension polynomial in $D$, supported in $r_i<.8D$, such that $$\inf_{v\in\mathcal V_i}\|v-\psi_i\|_{H^1}\le e^{-.58D}.
 \label{eq:wells-ritz-h1}$$ Its lowest Ritz value $\lambda_i^{\mathrm R}$ satisfies $$0\le\lambda_i^{\mathrm R}-\lambda_i\le C e^{-1.16D}.
 \label{eq:wells-ritz-bias}$$ The construction and constants are uniform over rational parameters throughout $[1,4]^m$.

Suppose the centers and the parameters in $[1,4]^m$ are rational, and all their numerators and denominators, as well as those of $q,q'$, have at most $B$ bits. Under the hypotheses of this section, a deterministic algorithm returns rational numbers $\ell_i\le\lambda_i\le u_i$ with $$u_i-\ell_i\le\varepsilon_D,\qquad
 \varepsilon_D=2^{-\lceil8D/5\rceil}<e^{-1.1D}.
 \label{eq:wells-oracle-precision}$$ Its bit complexity is polynomial in $D,m,B$. The bound is uniform over every rational sample in $[1,4]^m$; no spectral gap of a Ritz matrix is assumed.

At any fixed rational centers satisfying the hypotheses of this section, and with the integer charges in [eq:wells-charges] already fixed, one can compute rational $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_m\in[1,4]$ such that $$|\lambda_i+1/2|\le e^{-1.01D}\qquad(1\le i\le m). \label{eq:wells-tuned}$$ The algorithm is deterministic and polynomial in $D,m$ and the input bit lengths. Every parameter it samples or outputs has $O(D)$ fractional bits.

The zero-extended kernels $$G_D(z)=\frac{\chi(|z|/D)}{|z|},\qquad J_{D,\rho}(z)=\frac{\chi(|z|/D)}{|z-\rho e_z|}$$ are globally $C^2$, uniformly for $1\le\rho\le4$. For every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le2$, $$\|\partial^\alpha G_D\|_\infty+ \|\partial^\alpha J_{D,\rho}\|_\infty \le C D^{-1-|\alpha|}. \label{eq:capped-kernel-bounds}$$ Uniformly over all allowed secondary positions and rounded charges, $$\|W_i-W_i^*\|_\infty\le\frac{Cm^2}{D^2},\qquad |F_i(y)-F_i^*(y)|\le\frac{Cm^2}{D}\quad(r_i\le3D). \label{eq:surrogate-error}$$ Consequently, for tuned wells the relative formula [eq:relative-tail] holds with $F_i^*$ in place of $F_i$ and the same error bound $O(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}})$.

For tuned wells and every contact, $$B_{ij}=T_{ij}(X)
       \bigl(1+O(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}})\bigr).
 \label{eq:hole-surrogate-comparison}$$ The constants are uniform in $\rho_j\in[1,4]$.

Let $X^0=(Dp_i)_i$. For every contact, $$c e^{-D}\le T_{ij}(X^0)\le C D^2 e^{-D+Cm}.
 \label{eq:reference-hopping-bounds}$$

For $0<\epsilon<1/10$, one can compute a positive rational $\widehat I_{ij}$ satisfying $$\left|\log\frac{\widehat I_{ij}}{e^D T_{ij}(X^0)}\right|
   \le\epsilon
 \label{eq:reference-quadrature-accuracy}$$ by a deterministic algorithm polynomial in $D$, $m$, the bit lengths of the layout data, and $\epsilon^{-1}$. In particular the algorithm is polynomial in the source size when $D$ is a fixed polynomial and $\epsilon$ an inverse polynomial.

For distinct sites, $$B_{ij}-B_{ji}
   =(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)\langle\psi_j,\psi_i\rangle.
 \label{eq:hopping-orientation-identity}$$ For tuned wells and large $D$ under the stated separation bounds, $$|\langle\psi_j,\psi_i\rangle|\le e^{-0.85D},\qquad
 |B_{ij}-B_{ji}|\le2e^{-1.86D}.
 \label{eq:hopping-orientation-error}$$

Let the contact layout be as in Lemma 5, choose one orientation per contact, and let the prescribed rational hoppings satisfy $03. For inverse-polynomial $\tau$, there is a deterministic polynomial-time procedure that computes rational centers $X_i=Dp_i+s_i$ obeying $$S:=\max_i|s_i| \le Cm\bigl(m+\log D+\log(1/t_{\min})+1\bigr)+\tau. \label{eq:calibrated-displacement-size}$$ After applying Proposition 14 at these final centers, the resulting orbitals satisfy, on every chosen oriented contact, $$|Z_*B_{ij}-t_{ij}| \le C t_{ij}\mathcal E_{\mathrm{cal}}. \label{eq:calibrated-contact-error}$$ Here $D$ is taken sufficiently large for the hypotheses above and for $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{cal}}$ to be small. The reverse oriented attraction has an additional error at most $4e^{-0.86D}$ in the same rescaled units. No additional geometric equation for the reverse orientation is needed.

For the preceding parameters and sufficiently large $D$, $$\|A\psi_i\|_2\le e^{-.75D},\qquad
 \|G-I\|\le e^{-.85D}.
 \label{eq:continuum-residual-gram}$$ In particular $G$ is positive definite. The isometry $\mathcal J_0=\mathcal U G^{-1/2}$ has orthonormal columns $\omega_i=\mathcal J_0e_i$, spanning the same spatial orbital space. Its matrix satisfies $$\begin{aligned}
 \|Z_*\mathcal J_0^*A\mathcal J_0-\mathsf T\|
 &\le \delta_1, \label{eq:continuum-one-body-error}\\
 \delta_1
 &:=m\epsilon_{\mathrm{hop}}+Z_*e^{-1.01D}
       +CmZ_*e^{-1.1D}+CmZ_*e^{-1.6D}. \notag
\end{aligned}$$ If $P_0=\mathcal J_0\mathcal J_0^*$, then $$\|AP_0\|\le C\sqrt m\,e^{-.75D},
 \qquad
 \|\omega_i-\phi_i\|_{H^1}\le Cm/D.
 \label{eq:continuum-projected-residual}$$

There is a constant $g>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $D$, $$(I-P)A(I-P)\ge g(I-P).$$ The inequality holds on the full one-particle form domain, including functions supported between the nuclei or at infinity.

Uniformly over all normalized $u\in\operatorname{Ran}\Pi$, $$\sum_{\ell=1}^m\|\nabla_{y_\ell}u\|_2^2\le Cm,
 \qquad
 \|W_{\mathrm{ee}}\Pi\|\le Cm^2.
 \label{eq:continuum-fermion-hardy}$$ The constants do not depend on the dimension $\binom{2m}{m}$ of $\operatorname{Ran}\Pi$.

For sufficiently large $D$, let $E_\Pi=\min\operatorname{Spec}
(\Pi\mathcal H\Pi|_{\operatorname{Ran}\Pi})$. Then $$0\le E_\Pi-\inf\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal H
 \le e^{-1.2D}.
 \label{eq:continuum-leakage-error}$$ More explicitly, the upper bound can be taken to be $$C\left(m^{3/2}e^{-.75D}+m^2/Z_*\right)^2.$$

For sufficiently large $D$, $$\left\|W_{\mathrm{eff}}
       -U\sum_{i=1}^m n_{i\uparrow}n_{i\downarrow}\right\|
 \le \frac{Cm^5}{D},\qquad U=\frac58 .
 \label{eq:continuum-coulomb-error}$$
